reason: I'll build the artery first: the lining fits its inner surface, and the elastic wall should help it handle pulses.
expectation: I expect a lined artery with a strong, elastic wall; I don't know if it will need more parts.

alternatives.reason: The thin capillaries beside cells also look useful for exchange, but I'll start with the outward route.

effect: The lined arteries carry blood away from the heart, completing the outward-route goal. I'll work on exchange next.
reaction: The smooth lining and outward arrows matched what I expected.
reason: The thin capillary walls are shown close to body cells, so this should build the exchange area.
expectation: I expect capillaries positioned beside cells so materials can pass between blood and the cells.

alternatives.reason: The venous wall also needs a lining for the return route, but I'll make the exchange area first.

effect: The capillary bed shows oxygen and nutrients moving to cells and carbon dioxide moving toward blood, while blood cells stay inside. The exchange goal is complete.
reaction: The close-up made the exchange easier to picture.
reason: I'll line the venous wall to work toward the remaining return-route goal. The picture shows that its inner surface needs a lining.
expectation: I expect a lined vein, but it will probably still need the one-way valve flaps.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the artery to the capillary bed seems useful, but I want to prepare the return route first.

effect: The lining made thin-walled veins that point back toward the heart; they still need valves for the return-route goal.
reaction: The result matched what I expected.
reason: The valve flaps fit the veins and should help keep blood moving one way.
expectation: I expect veins with valves that open for forward flow and close against backward flow.

alternatives.reason: Joining the arteries and capillary bed also seems useful, but I'll finish the return route first.

effect: The valves complete the return route, and the picture shows a contracting muscle helping push blood forward. Now the three routes need joining.
reaction: The muscle squeezing the vein was a useful detail I hadn't expected.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and joining arteries to the capillary bed starts connecting the routes.
expectation: I expect blood to have a route from the arteries into the capillaries; the veins may need connecting afterward.

effect: The artery now branches into capillaries, leaving the return side open for the veins.
reaction: The branching route makes the connection easy to picture.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the venous return should connect to the open collecting ends.
expectation: I expect a joined route from arteries through capillaries and back toward the heart through veins.

effect: The completed network connects arteries, capillaries and veins into a route away from and back toward the heart. All chapter goals are complete.
reaction: Seeing the separate routes join into one continuous path was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the capillary bed was most worthwhile: it showed what moves between blood and body cells and what stays inside the vessels.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the lining to the veins felt a little repetitive after lining the artery, though its purpose was clear.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected the picture to show a contracting muscle squeezing a vein to help move blood past the valves.

arbitrary.text: None felt particularly arbitrary. The pictures explained the parts, although the last two combinations were the only options offered rather than discoveries I made independently.

continue.text: I would probably continue: connecting the separate vessel routes was satisfying, and the capillary exchange picture made me curious about how other systems work together.
